title: Finite projective-space embeddings of a fibre product and its closed models
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $f:X\to S$ a separated morphism of schemes, meaning that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $I$ be a finite nonempty set, $n\geq0$, and for each $i\in I$ let $q_i:Y_i\to X$ be a morphism with a closed immersion $e_i:Y_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ over $S$ for the structure map $fq_i$ [def-kun-projective]. Form $P=\prod_{i\in I,X}Y_i$ with structure map $r:P\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and put $N=(n+1)^{|I|}-1$. The canonical map $P\to\prod_{i\in I,S}Y_i$, specified by its projections, is a closed immersion. There is a closed immersion $e_P:P\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ over $S$. For every closed immersion $c:T\hookrightarrow P$, put $q=rc:T\to X$. There exist closed immersions $e_T:T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ over $S$ and $d_T:T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_X$ over $X$, with structural projections equal to $fq$ and $q$, respectively. Thus $P\to S$, $T\to S$ and $q$ are projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective], are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and are of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The schemes $P$ and $T$ are Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. If there is a dense open $V\subset X$ such that $q^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-open-immersion], then $q$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. No integrality or group action is assumed; $T$ may be empty when the last extra hypothesis is absent.

source.place: Tag 01WD, lemma-segre-embedding; schemes.tex Tag 01KR, lemma-fibre-product-after-map; morphisms.tex Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence (closed-graph proof in the finite-space convention), Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper, and Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian. Returned proof steps 3 and 8 and the projective ambient Noetherianity part of step 6.

proof.text:
Enumerate $I=\{1,\ldots,m\}$, where $m\geq1$. For $1\leq j\leq m$ put $A_j=\prod_{i\leq j,X}Y_i$ and $B_j=\prod_{i\leq j,S}Y_i$, using [def-pc-fibre-product], with $r_j:A_j\to X$ the common composite of their projections with the $q_i$. Their $S$-structure maps are $fr_j$ and the common composite on $B_j$. We prove inductively that the map $h_j:A_j\to B_j$ with the given projections is a closed immersion. For $j=1$ it is the identity, which is a closed immersion directly from [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For the induction step factor $h_{j+1}$ as
$$A_j\times_XY_{j+1}\longrightarrow A_j\times_SY_{j+1}\xrightarrow{h_j\times\mathrm{id}}B_j\times_SY_{j+1}.$$
The first arrow is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-change-of-base-closed-immersion], applied to $A_j\to X$, $q_{j+1}$ and the separated map $f:X\to S$. The second is a base change of $h_j$ along $B_j\times_SY_{j+1}\to B_j$, hence is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Compose by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]. Both arrows have the prescribed projections, so their composite is $h_{j+1}$ by the fibre-product universal property. The same universal property identifies $A_m$ and $B_m$ with the stated finite products, preserving every projection; hence the map at $j=m$ is the stated canonical map $P\to\prod_{i\in I,S}Y_i$ over $S$.

source.place: Tag 01KR, lemma-fibre-product-after-map; finite induction using morphisms.tex Tags 01QR and 01QS, lemma-base-change-closed-immersion and lemma-composition-closed-immersion.

proof.text:
Construct by induction a closed immersion $b_j:B_j\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{M_j}_S$ over $S$, where $M_j=(n+1)^j-1$. Start with $b_1=e_1$. Given $b_j$, the map
$$B_j\times_SY_{j+1}\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{M_j}_S\times_SY_{j+1}\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{M_j}_S\times_S\mathbf P^n_S$$
has first arrow the base change of $b_j$ along $\mathbf P^{M_j}_S\times_SY_{j+1}\to\mathbf P^{M_j}_S$, and second arrow the base change of $e_{j+1}$ along $\mathbf P^{M_j}_S\times_S\mathbf P^n_S\to\mathbf P^n_S$. It is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]. Compose with the binary Segre closed immersion of [lem-chow-segre]. Its target dimension is $(M_j+1)(n+1)-1=(n+1)^{j+1}-1$. All arrows are over $S$; the base-change identifications are the isomorphisms with identical projections supplied by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $b_m$ has target $\mathbf P^N_S$. Compose $h_m$ with $b_m$, using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], to obtain $e_P$ over $S$ with projection $fr$.

source.place: Tag 01WD, lemma-segre-embedding, iterated binary embedding; morphisms.tex Tags 01QR and 01QS for the product of the given embeddings.

proof.text: For the arbitrary closed immersion $c:T\hookrightarrow P$, set $e_T=e_Pc$. It is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], and its structural projection is $(fr)c=fq$. Hence $P\to S$ and $T\to S$ are projective by [def-kun-projective]. For $d_T$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-change-of-base-closed-immersion] to $q:T\to X$, $\mathrm{id}_X$ and the separated map $f$: the map $T\times_XX\to T\times_SX$ is a closed immersion. The projection $T\times_XX\to T$ is an isomorphism with inverse $(\mathrm{id}_T,q)$ by [def-pc-fibre-product], so the graph $\gamma=(\mathrm{id}_T,q):T\to T\times_SX$ is a closed immersion. The map $k=e_T\times_S\mathrm{id}_X:T\times_SX\to\mathbf P^N_S\times_SX$ is the base change of $e_T$ along the first projection $\mathbf P^N_S\times_SX\to\mathbf P^N_S$ (the two fibre products are identified by maps with the same projections [def-pc-fibre-product]), hence a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Then $k\gamma=(e_T,q)$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], with second projection $q$. By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] for $f$ and the coordinate set $\{0,\ldots,N\}$, together with the interchange of factors [def-pc-fibre-product], $\mathbf P^N_S\times_SX\cong\mathbf P^N_X$ over $X$, and these are the projective spaces of [def-kun-projective]. A closed immersion followed by an isomorphism is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This gives $d_T:T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_X$ over $X$ with the same $N$ and structural projection $q$, i.e. projectivity of $q$ in the finite-space convention. No flatness or finite-type hypothesis on $X$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence, closed-graph proof (X -> X x_S Y -> P x_S Y) written out for the finite projective-space embedding; schemes.tex Tag 01KR, lemma-fibre-product-after-map; morphisms.tex Tags 01QR, 01QS.

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] to each of $P\to S$, $T\to S$, and $q:T\to X$. They are proper. Each is therefore of finite type, since finite type is part of the definition [def-weil-proper-morphism]. No finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ was used.

source.place: Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper, and the definition of properness.

proof.text: The only ideals of the field $k$ are $(0)$ and $(1)$: an ideal containing $a\ne0$ contains $a^{-1}a=1$ [def-weil-field]. They are finitely generated, so $k$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The one-chart affine cover of $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, with coordinate ring $k$, proves that $S$ is locally Noetherian [def-weil-affine-spectrum, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Its underlying space has one point [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and every open cover contains a member containing that point, so it is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Thus $S$ is Noetherian in the stated convention.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian, base hypothesis; field case from the definitions, and Properties Tag 01OV for Noetherian schemes.

proof.text: Both $P\to S$ and $T\to S$ are of finite type by step 4, and $S$ is Noetherian by step 5. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to each. This proves that $P$ and $T$ are locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, exactly the required Noetherianity. This argument also applies when $T$ is empty.

Finally suppose $V\subset X$ is dense open and $q^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism. Then $V\subset q(T)$. Properness of $q$ means it is universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]; taking the identity base change shows that $q$ is closed. In particular $q(T)$ is closed in $X$, since $T$ is closed in itself. As it contains $V$, it contains its closure $X$. Thus every point of $X$ is the image of a point of $T$, which is surjectivity [def-weil-surjective-morphism].
